name: Patdiam Jewellery Limited
classification: Hold for evidence / no favourable ranking
summary: HOLD FOR EVIDENCE, not an integrity-fail or an instruction to sell. Patdiam is a small export manufacturer with real operations and a long reported profit history, but accounting earnings have not translated reliably into distributable cash. Parent revenue rose to ₹171.30 crore in FY2026, while the group reported ₹173.1229 crore revenue and ₹16.5956 crore attributable PAT. These are different perimeters, not interchangeable growth series. Parent cumulative FY2023–FY2026 CFO was only ₹2.4346 crore against ₹42.4213 crore PAT. Its latest cash improvement was partly financed by supplier balances and customer advances. A new overseas subsidiary and ₹23.10 crore CWIP now increase execution and funding questions. At the expressly assumed ₹340 price, market capitalization is ₹146.778 crore and reported group P/E about 8.84 x, but those apparent bargains capitalize sizeable FX gains. G2 financial reliability, G3 funding and G4 tradability are Hold; G1 integrity/minority protection is Conditional. Ordinary returns, current-price-dependent factors and overall IAS are unscored. No favorable ranking is earned by conditional bull upside. The key next evidence is a reconciled consolidation and cash-flow package, sanctioned facility renewals, project completion budget, and actual BSE trade/restriction data. This is research under a nominal pretax 15% five-year hurdle, not personalized allocation advice.

sections.title: Identity, listing and research boundaries
sections.text: The exact issuer is Patdiam Jewellery Limited, CIN L36911MH1999PLC120537, ISIN INE473T01011, BSE code 539401, interop symbol PJL$, SME security series SM. The 19 October 2026 exchange interop master supports 4,317,000 issued shares and a 750-share board lot. Its appearance in an NSE interop file does not make it an NSE-listed stock. Financial observations are considered through 20 October 2026, normally using 19 October as the market reference. The latest audited statements are 31 March 2026; the latest verified interim is 30 September 2025 and there is no invented September 2026 TTM. The 5 October 2026 ₹340/750 shares row is a dated secondary observation, not a verified current exchange price. Official BSE bhavcopy access returned 403. The valid shared 60-session NSE files do not establish BSE trades; absence is not a zero-volume day. The March 2026 shareholding filing shows 74.15% promoters and 25.85% public, with no disclosed promoter encumbrance, warrants or convertibles in that filing. Subsequent changes, current circuits, surveillance and depth remain unverified. The ₹500,000 position is an illustrative framework test only: one lot at the scenario price costs₹255,000, while two lots cost₹510,000. No claim of suitability or executable allocation is made.

sections.title: Business model, revenue and unit economics
sections.text: The parent designs and manufactures diamond-studded gold and silver jewellery at SEEPZ for export buyers. FY2026 export sales were ₹167.6699 crore, approximately 97.9% of parent operations revenue; local sales were ₹3.6301 crore. Its economic engine is design/conversion value added and reliable delivery, not the gross gold and diamond content invoiced to customers. Reported revenue mixes metal prices, diamond mix, currency translation, customer demand and quantities. Neither units, standardized metal weight, realized conversion spreads, customer-level retention nor constant-currency sales were disclosed sufficiently to isolate organic growth. Materials plus traded goods and inventory changes provide only a material-margin proxy, because labour and subcontracting sit elsewhere. It must not be labelled audited gross margin. Receivables can remain outstanding while bullion, labour and suppliers require cash. Customer advances and export credit partially finance this cycle but are not free permanent equity. A US distribution presence may improve customer access while adding inventory, payroll, goodwill and foreign cash-location risk. The new wholly owned Ancora Design Trading(s) LLC is not the separately named related-party Ancora Designs LLC, nor the two old disputed American investments. Group revenue adds only ₹1.8229 crore above parent revenue after eliminations, not the subsidiary’s entire reported turnover as external organic growth. Customer concentration and binding order-book coverage remain ND.

sections.title: Industry structure, peers and competitive advantage
sections.text: Demand is discretionary, export-oriented and exposed to US retailers’ inventory cycles, tariffs and currency. Gold and diamond price increases can lift rupee turnover without more units or better conversion economics; falling diamond values can impair inventory realization. CRISIL describes intense competition and moderate pricing power, consistent with a manufacturing supplier rather than a demonstrated consumer brand franchise. Product quality, experienced promoters, design capability and long customer relationships can support repeat business. They are not evidence of switching costs, protected intellectual property or durable price-setting. Goldiam is a useful diamond-jewellery manufacturing/export comparator; Renaissance Global explicitly separates customer OEM/private-label activity from owned/licensed brands; Silgo is a silver design/manufacturing and retail/wholesale comparator. Their products, brand ownership, channel mix and scale differ materially, so no mechanical peer P/E discount proves value. The qualitative moat assessment uses primary business descriptions, not promotional claims as fact. No verified evidence establishes Patdiam’s customer churn, share gains, premium pricing or brand pull. A strong FY2025 rebound can coexist with weak structural cash returns. The reasonable base is a competitive exporter with execution capabilities, not a monopolistic niche. Re-rate the moat only after repeat customer cohorts, conversion-margin stability through metal/FX cycles and demonstrated return on the enlarged capital base.

sections.title: Historical growth, normalization and organic bridge
sections.text: The complete embedded history covers FY2020–FY2026 parent observations, with FY2020–FY2021 from primary audited results, FY2022 from FY2023 audited comparatives and FY2023–FY2026 from full annual reports. The website link labelled AnnualReport 2022 is byte-identical to FY2023 and does not create extra audit coverage. Revenue was approximately₹105.73 crore in FY2022, ₹105.68 crore in FY2023 and ₹103.40 crore in FY2024 before jumping to₹157.76 crore and₹171.30 crore. Thus COVID-low-base CAGR and the one-year rebound are poor substitutes for steady organic growth. H1FY2026 revenue declined roughly 2.1% and PAT was broadly flat versus H1FY2025; most annual FY2026 profit arose in the derived second half. There is no unsupported seasonality adjustment or September 2026 estimate. Other income rose to₹8.8752 crore in the parent, chiefly₹8.8154 crore FX gains, versus₹3.4805 crore other income in FY2025. The cash flow reverses₹5.6403 crore unrealized FX. Operating EBIT is therefore shown excluding all other income, with a transparent sensitivity because realized FX can legitimately belong to exporter economics. The report does not claim every FX gain is exceptional. Organic revenue remains unscored until volume, metal-price/pass-through, currency and scope bridges are supplied. FY2026 consolidated figures are separate and not appended to parent CAGR or cumulative cash conversion.

sections.title: Capital allocation and incremental returns
sections.text: Capital intensity increased sharply: parent PPE plus CWIP rose to₹33.8309 crore, including₹23.10 crore work in progress, and group goodwill carries₹4.7279 crore after amortization. Parent cash capex was₹24.0130 crore in FY2026 and₹7.9147 crore in FY2025; the group first-year cash-flow presentation reports₹28.9773 crore purchases, but scope/opening adjustments prevent a simple like-for-like bridge. The₹2.5728 crore subsidiary subscription is a parent investing outflow, not automatically cash spent outside the consolidated group. No duplicate subsidiary subscription is charged to group forecast cash. Existing CWIP is already funded historical capital and is not charged again as future capex; remaining commitments and commissioning dates are ND, so the model states alternative future capex budgets. The stable parent FY2022–FY2025 bridge excludes nonoperating cash/investments from financing-derived invested capital and removes other income from NOPAT at a standardized 25% tax rate. Incremental NOPAT of approximately₹5.1050 crore over incremental capital₹48.7873 crore implies about 10.46%, below the explicitly assumed 12–16% capital-cost range. This is a broad economic proxy, not precise project IRR, and includes working-capital/tax timing. The FY2023–FY2026 bridge is also shown but is weakened by overseas scope and uncommissioned capital. Current reported ROCE alone does not earn a high CAP score. No additional operating-property value is added on top of earnings EV.

sections.title: Cash conversion, inventory, ageing and FX
sections.text: Persistent cash weakness is measurable rather than inferred from one bad year. Parent CFO was negative in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 before reaching₹14.1594 crore in FY2026. FY2025 CFO also benefited from₹11.1618 crore loans/advances release, so it understates underlying operating absorption; after-interest cash proxies are shown separately without asserting that all advances are nonoperating. FY2023–FY2026 cumulative CFO/PAT is only about 5.7%; the longer FY2022–FY2026 series is better but still well below full profit conversion. FY2026 parent trade receivables reached₹90.0091 crore and inventory₹38.2629 crore; over-six-month receivables total₹14.7324 crore, including₹8.5170 crore older than one year. Ageing and subsequent receipts matter more than management’s good/deemed-good designation. Supplier payables and customer advances, the latter₹9.0869 crore, helped finance the latest cash improvement. Group inventory rises to₹58.6187 crore while receivables fall to₹52.3128 crore after scope/eliminations, so naive consolidated-day improvements are not proven collection efficiency. CARO reports inventory differences below 10% for each class, not zero discrepancies. Parent net disclosed unhedged USD exposure is approximately₹59.1021 crore after relevant receivables, creditors, advances and packing credit; a 5% INR appreciation is a₹2.9551 crore pretax sensitivity before behaviour/hedges, not a prediction. Group FX column headings are duplicated and cannot be assumed perfectly reconciled. Cumulative cash weakness triggers the framework GQS ceiling of 5 even though missing organic REV leaves GQS itself NS.

sections.title: Balance sheet, funding and contingent obligations
sections.text: FY2026 consolidated gross debt is₹27.4991 crore, including₹15.5318 crore packing credit,₹6.90 crore related-party short-term loans and current/long-term bank and vehicle term debt. Group cash/bank is₹6.0614 crore; excluding all₹0.5880 crore deposits leaves a conservative₹5.4734 crore opening cash proxy. Parent cash after the same exclusion is only₹0.2990 crore, with roughly₹5.17 crore of the residual located in the new foreign subsidiary. Full ownership does not prove immediate remittance or legal/economic fungibility. CRISIL’s 17 September 2026 B+/Stable/A4 issuer-not-cooperating action follows requests for information and replaces the prior BB+/A4+ assessment; it is not a finding of default. ₹21 crore rated limits are not authenticated renewed availability. Nominal limits less disclosed working-capital draws are not modelled as free incremental headroom. The model assumes existing lines/related loans roll in its conditional base, then explicitly stresses nonrenewal and repayment. Legacy tax₹3.9504 crore, statutory₹0.1207 crore, employee₹1.0260 crore and other long-term₹2.4522 crore obligations are excluded from target operating working capital and settled once. A₹12 crore guarantee for a related firm and₹0.2138 crore disputed tax are stress calls, not asserted existing borrowings. G3 Hold reflects changed scale, noncooperation, debt rollover and cash location together, not merely absence of private daily bank statements. Model reserve breaches are not historical defaults.

sections.title: Governance, related parties and minority protection
sections.text: Promoters control 74.15% at March 2026, with no disclosed pledge in the reviewed aggregate filing. Control aligns some operating interests but leaves minority investors dependent on board discipline around related-party sourcing, funding and guarantees. Group related-party purchases include₹49.0408 crore from Patdiam LLP,₹2.7954 crore from Patdiam Jewels and₹3.8571 crore from Ancora Designs LLC. Their corresponding balances and lending relationships are material; the similarly named related counterparty must not be silently merged with the newly consolidated US subsidiary. The₹12 crore related-firm corporate guarantee can transfer risk without adding group revenue. Long-held US investments of approximately₹0.9256 crore in Americas Value Channel and Gem Media remain carried despite losses, litigation and an unfulfilled historic exit arrangement. CARO expressly calls those investments prejudicial to the company’s interests. The model assigns them no recovered value, without treating a contested claim as proven fraud. Secretarial reporting notes delayed disclosure of the new subsidiary’s incorporation, and FY2026 results were delayed while audit work remained incomplete. Conversely, the main statutory opinions are unmodified, the reviewed statements report no bank default and the shareholding filing does not show promoter encumbrance. These counterweights justify G1 Conditional rather than an unsupported integrity Fail. FY2027 auditor succession appears an ordinary tenure replacement in discovery material, not verified misconduct; no allegation is inferred from a change alone.

sections.title: Audit, accounting reliability and forensic overlay
sections.text: Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not Ind AS, govern these statements. Main opinions do not resolve annexure inconsistencies. Parent CARO internal-audit clause xiv(a) describes a commensurate system, while xiv(b) says none was established. The IFC basis mentions an adverse audit opinion but the actual opinion concludes adequate/effective controls. Similar contradictions recur in prior reports; they should be clarified, not relabelled conclusively adverse or dismissed as immaterial boilerplate. Consolidated CARO says no adverse parent remarks despite the standalone prejudicial-investment finding. Group IFC wording refers to India-incorporated entities and an Indian subsidiary although the disclosed sole subsidiary is in the USA; it cannot establish clean US-component controls. The first consolidated cash-flow statement sets prior figures to zero, inserts₹60.6831 crore first-preparation adjustment and reports₹8.6976 crore CFO. Note 35 nevertheless says consolidated cash flow is not presented. These impair comparability and call for a reconciled opening/consolidation bridge. AOC-I translated closing-rate subsidiary turnover/PAT/assets differ from component-audit figures; exchange translation may explain this and no misstatement is assumed. FY2024 bank-note cash₹3.4780 crore versus CFO cash₹3.3498 crore also lacks a clear reviewed maturity bridge. Quarterly bank returns reportedly agree with books, and audit-trail software reportedly operated without tampering; neither proves collections or offsets the specific contradictions. G2 Hold blocks a favourable quality or investment ranking pending reconciliation, without asserting fabricated accounts.

sections.title: Forward operating cases and dated funding model
sections.text: Forecasts start 31 March 2026, bridge to 19 October 2026 entry, then fiscal year ends through 31 March 2031 and 19 October 2031 exit. Exact calendar days use 365.25 for investment annualization. Every dated row shows cash profits, operating working-capital investment, capex, interest, legacy liabilities, principal, cash and reserve. FY2032 run-rate earnings value the continuing business at exit; only cash earned before exit is included and no post-exit financing supports the forecast. The base uses 6%,8%,8%,7%,6%,5% successive fiscal growth,8% operating margin excluding other income,115 receivable/175 inventory/85 payable/19 customer-advance days, and future capex₹4 crore then₹3 crore annually. Bull assumes stronger growth,10% margin and more efficient working capital; bear combines demand contraction,5% margin, slower collections/inventory, a guarantee call, receivable loss and related-loan repayment. These are disclosed analyst scenarios, not order-book forecasts. A₹2 crore cash reserve is selected, with₹0.25/1/2/4 crore sensitivity. In base, modelled pre-entry cash drops below reserve and later troughs near₹0.30 crore, suppressing no-rescue returns despite recovery later. The bull is conditionally funded only under cash-fungibility/rollover assumptions. All ordinary outputs remain null because current funding is not authenticated. The explicit bear rescue issues whole shares before each interval’s immediate stress uses and closing reserve shortfall at 20% below scenario price, with 3% costs, and separately shows dilution versus share-count expansion. It is not an expected or approved capital raise. Remaining bank and car term debt is conservatively repaid in full on 30 November 2029, including a maturity balloon, rather than silently carried beyond maturity. Stress guarantee/related-demand uses occur 1 April 2026 before subsequent receipts; old tax is assumed paid 30 September 2026, with other flows uniform between dated events.

sections.title: Valuation, price-implied expectations and entry discipline
sections.text: ₹340 is a scenario assumption tied to a 5 October secondary row, not an authenticated 19 October executable quote. On that assumption, reported group P/E appears low, but enterprise value excluding all deposits is approximately₹168.8 crore against normalized operating EBIT₹15.4193 crore, roughly 10.95 x. Reported PAT includes FX and is not the same as owner cash flow. Model exit values use 6 x/8 x/10 x normalized EBIT, deduct debt and residual legacy claims, and add only cash above an untouched operating reserve. Goodwill, operating property, inventory and existing CWIP receive no separate additive value. The distressed US investment receives no recovered value. A separate book-value haircut exercise stresses receivables, inventory, CWIP, goodwill and disputed investments without calling net assets a liquidation floor. No-rescue bear and base terminal prices, IRRs and 12/15/18% hurdle entries are null after cash-floor breaches, including those before entry. Conditional bull results are not a buy recommendation or IAS substitute. Two-way working-capital/multiple and capex/reserve matrices show that financing assumptions can dominate optical valuation. Reverse-growth solving accepts only a finite funded crossing and validates its residual; where none exists, no required growth or endpoint estimate is reported. R and P remain NS because quote/funding deficiencies preclude current executable return and implied-expectation claims. A lower price alone cannot cure financial reliability, cash fungibility or tradability holds. Entry friction of 0/1% and exit impact of 0/5/10% are explicitly assumed sensitivities on funded conditional and rescue outcomes, not observed spreads. A 10x share-price gain in five years would require about 58.5% annual appreciation, far above the conditional bull case; no substantiated multibagger case is established.

sections.title: Liquidity, market implementation and downside
sections.text: The verified board lot is 750 shares. At₹340, a₹500,000 reference position rounds down to 750 shares/₹255,000 or up to 1,500 shares/₹510,000. The choice is not innocuous for a small portfolio. Secondary history shows isolated 750-share days and some 2,250-share days; with 5% participation, even a 2,250-share day permits 112.5 shares before lot rounding, hence zero executable whole lots under that rule. This is an illustrative capacity constraint, not a complete sixty-session liquidity study. Exact 20/60-session mean and median traded value, counted zero-trade sessions, spread, order-book depth, current circuits and surveillance status remain ND because a primary BSE series was not obtained. A missing NSE row is not evidence of no BSE trade. L is NS rather than a fabricated numeric score; G4 Hold prevents implementation. The capital-loss case is broader than mark-to-market volatility: inventory markdowns, long-dated debtor losses, a related guarantee call, restricted foreign cash, bank nonrenewal and a deeply discounted rescue can permanently dilute equity. The model stresses parent-only cash, partial subsidiary access, related-loan repayment and bank nonrenewal separately. D is assessed conservatively from those mechanisms, while distinguishing an analyst-selected cash reserve from insolvency law. Neither historical profit nor book equity guarantees an exit at the displayed secondary quote.

sections.title: Monitoring, catalysts, disconfirming evidence and questions
sections.text: Reconsider the Hold only when specific evidence improves. First obtain an auditor/company explanation reconciling parent CARO/IFC, consolidated scope wording, opening cash and the first-preparation adjustment, plus the subsidiary balance sheet and cash-location/elimination bridge. Second obtain facility renewal dates, sanctioned draw availability, covenants, lender balances, related-loan maturity terms and remaining CWIP commitments/commissioning economics. Third demand receivable ageing roll-forward and subsequent collections, inventory ageing/valuation provisions, customer concentration and the split of quantity, metal-price, FX and acquired/distribution scope growth. Fourth authenticate the actual current BSE quote, corporate actions, lot, restrictions and complete 60-session liquidity before implementation. Potential positive catalysts are cash collections, commissioned capacity earning returns above capital cost, recurring conversion margin without FX support, rating cooperation restored and demonstrably funded foreign distribution. Negative triggers include ageing deterioration, persistent supplier/customer-advance dependence, additional group guarantees, related-party exposure growth, further reporting delays or debt nonrenewal. A clean main opinion alone is not sufficient disconfirmation; conversely an explained translation/perimeter bridge, bank-confirmed funding and strong subsequent receipts should reduce penalties rather than preserve suspicion. No management response resolving these specific items was found by the cutoff. No unsupported fraud, default or customer-loss assertion is made. Review the next half-year filing, auditor clarifications and credit action when actually available, without assuming their outcome.

sections.title: Factor audit, gates, limitations and conclusion
sections.text: The 13 factor audit below preserves evidence, counterevidence, confidence and change conditions rather than treating scores as facts. GOV4, MOAT4, DUR4, CAP4, CASH2, BAL4, EXEC4, EARN4 and D3 are judgement-based; REV, R, P and L are NS where critical inputs are unresolved. BQS and GQS therefore remain NS with explicit missing-factor bounds, not neutral substitutions. The persistent CASH2 finding caps diagnostic GQS upside at 5; the uncapped bound is still retained. IAS is NS and ineligible for favourable investment ranking under G2/G3/G4 Hold. Decimal weights are unchanged from frameworkv 3.0 and one-decimal displays use HALF_UP; any IAS arithmetic would use unrounded BQS. Complete annual data, interim observations, assumptions, dated scenario rows, sensitivity matrices, reverse-solver scans and all source-register entries are embedded in the canonical record. Financial estimates use disclosed-lakh precision converted to crore, so immaterial rounding differences are not evidence of wrongdoing. The source-safe reproduction preserves factual extracts and calculation logic, not the copyrighted reports themselves, and cannot newly authenticate a missing market price or missing lender commitment. The practical conclusion is an evidence watchlist with no normal entry range today. It can become investable research only if business cash generation, reliability, funding and actual market access converge, not merely because trailing P/E looks cheap. Joint ±1 GOV/CAP scoring sensitivity preserves NS, the GQS ceiling and gate exclusions. Evidence coverage is separately disclosed: BQS scored weight 88%, GQS 60%, direct IAS 20% (42% including underlying scored BQS factors), not a claim of reliability. If the hypothetical GOV3 were supported by sufficient adverse evidence, the sensitivity separately applies the governance cap of3 to BQS/IAS diagnostic bounds and hypothetical Avoid-governance, while retaining raw bounds and NS points. This does not change the actual GOV4 assessment.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Material connected exposures, old prejudicial investments and disclosure weaknesses; insufficient evidence for proven fraud/integrity fail.
gates.clearance: Resolved independent governance/audit explanation and controlled related exposures.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Unresolved recurring CARO/IFC contradictions, foreign-component scope wording and first-year consolidation/cash-flow ambiguity.
gates.clearance: Auditor-backed clean reconciliation of scope, cash, opening entries and annexures.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Post-expansion current renewals/cash fungibility unverified after issuer noncooperation; base conditionalreserve2crore cash floor breaches. Not an assertion of historical default.
gates.clearance: Renewed committed lines, debt terms, accessible cash and completion-cost bridge demonstrate financeability.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: 750sharelot and thin dated observations; complete primaryBSEvolume, spread, restrictions and cutoffprice absent.
gates.clearance: Verify current executable quote, restrictions and wholelot capacity.

GOV.name: Governance and minority protection
GOV.rationale: Material related-party sourcing,₹12crore related guarantee and prejudicial historic US investments; recurring reporting/control inconsistencies.
GOV.counterevidence: No reviewed payment default; main audit unmodified; promoter pledge not disclosed.
GOV.raise_conditions: Require board and auditor explanations, arm’s-length evidence and declining connected exposures.
GOV.lower_conditions: Any substantiated diversion, unexplained guarantee expansion or adverse collections would lower.

MOAT.name: Moat and pricing power
MOAT.rationale: Design/manufacturing capability and export experience but intense competition/moderate price power. No switching-cost or brand-premium proof.
MOAT.counterevidence: Repeat customer relationships and a long operating history may help conversion demand.
MOAT.raise_conditions: Improve on documented retention, price premia and margin resilience across cycles.
MOAT.lower_conditions: Loss of repeat demand, margin erosion or dependence would lower.

REV.name: Organic revenue growth
REV.rationale: Nominal growth is measurable but quantities, metal pass-through, constant-currency and new-distributor scope bridge are missing.
REV.counterevidence: FY2025 rebound and FY2026 continued revenue expansion are real reported outcomes.
REV.raise_conditions: Score only after a defensible like-for-like organic bridge; unchanged framework thresholds apply.
REV.lower_conditions: Do not fill missing organic growth with nominal CAGR or neutral5.

DUR.name: Growth durability
DUR.rationale: Discretionary export demand, tariffs, concentrated channels and unknown customer cohorts weaken visibility.
DUR.counterevidence: Established operations and international distribution may support future repeat orders.
DUR.raise_conditions: Longer customer cohorts, profitable capacity utilization and diversification would improve.
DUR.lower_conditions: Order cancellations, receivable ageing and new-market losses would weaken.

CAP.name: Incremental capital returns
CAP.rationale: Stable parentFY2022–FY2025 normalized incrementalNOPAT/capital≈10.46%, below assumed12–16% capital cost; later expansion raises lag risk.
CAP.counterevidence: Denominator includes growth-stage capital and tax timing; CWIP can earn future returns.
CAP.raise_conditions: Operating-side/cash bridge and commissioned project returns above cost would improve.
CAP.lower_conditions: Persistent idle capacity, more working capital or impaired goodwill would lower.

CASH.name: Cash realization
CASH.rationale: Three consecutive negative parentCFO years; FY2023–FY2026 cumulativeCFO/PAT≈5.7%; FY2025 advance release and FY2026 supplier/customer funding inflate apparent conversion.
CASH.counterevidence: FY2022 generated strong cash and FY2026 reportedCFO improved.
CASH.raise_conditions: Sustained post-interestCFO/PAT and collections without advances/payables leverage would improve.
CASH.lower_conditions: Further debtor ageing, inventory write-offs or dependence on related funding would lower.

BAL.name: Balance-sheet resilience
BAL.rationale: Borrowing, CWIP and contingent guarantees increased; most group cash is outside the parent and renewal information is weak.
BAL.counterevidence: Book equity is positive, debt not enormous against gross assets, and no historical default is established.
BAL.raise_conditions: Renewed committed facilities, parent-accessible cash and lower guarantee/debt would improve.
BAL.lower_conditions: Actual nonrenewal, guarantee crystallization or impairment would lower.

EXEC.name: Execution and disclosure
EXEC.rationale: Long operating record offset by late results/subsidiary disclosure, unclear expansion economics and recurring annexure inconsistency.
EXEC.counterevidence: Revenue/pat history exists and subsidiary was consolidated; delayed audit eventually completed.
EXEC.raise_conditions: On-time coherent reports and funded commissioning with cash results would improve.
EXEC.lower_conditions: Missed budgets, further filing delays or unexplained scope changes would lower.

EARN.name: Earnings growth quality
EARN.rationale: Profit growth contains substantial unrealized and realizedFX; parentH1FY2026 PAT flat and annual growthH2-heavy.
EARN.counterevidence: Manufacturing operatingEBIT remains positive after removing allotherincome, an intentionally conservative normalization.
EARN.raise_conditions: Stable conversionmargin, normalizedPAT and cash without FX uplift would improve.
EARN.lower_conditions: FX reversal, inventory/receivable loss or financing costs outgrowing margins would lower.

R.name: Prospective shareholder return
R.rationale: Current price/funding not authenticated; base/bear no-rescue cash floors breached, so returns are null.
R.counterevidence: Bull conditionally funds and offers upside, but is not a valid base estimate.
R.raise_conditions: Verify executable price and financeable per-share cash path before scoring.
R.lower_conditions: No present score or neutral substitution.

D.name: Downside and permanent-loss risk
D.rationale: Guarantee call, inventory/receivable loss and working-capital demand can require heavily dilutive rescue; secondary liquidity is poor.
D.counterevidence: Tangible assets and profitable operation provide some cushion, but recoveries are uncertain.
D.raise_conditions: Improve with reduced connected guarantees, collections, firm funding and proven inventory realization.
D.lower_conditions: Confirmed default, erosion or rescue at punitive prices would lower.

P.name: Price-implied expectations
P.rationale: Scenario₹340 is not a cutoff quote; no verified funded reverse-growth root supports an executable expectations claim.
P.counterevidence: Reported multiple looks modest but normalizedEBIT/ownercash are less cheap.
P.raise_conditions: Authenticate quote and funded margin/growth/working-capital bridge, then rerun solver.
P.lower_conditions: Never report an unbracketed search endpoint as required growth.

L.name: Liquidity and implementability
L.rationale: 750sharelot confirmed; full BSE20/60-session volume, spread and restrictions ND. Wholelot capacity can be zero on observed small-volume days.
L.counterevidence: There are dated secondary traded rows, not evidence of a completely untradeable security.
L.lower_conditions: Missing exchange rows cannot become zero sessions or a fabricated numerical score.
